text:
incident-bot: ALERT: High GPU allocation failures in us-west-2 (region: us-west-2). Affected pool: dedicated-gpu-pool-3. 95% of allocation requests failing since 02:17 UTC. Severity: P1. Paging oncall: @maria :rotating_light:

maria: saw it, i'm oncall. digging into allocation errors now.

maria: logs show OOM/insufficient resources from node plugin, trying quick restart of autoscaler controller to see if it's stuck.

ops-bot: deploy started: autoscaler-controller v3.9.2 -> v3.9.3 by maria — /deploy autoscaler-controller --canary

dan: tagging in from runtime. can we confirm if this is autoscaler or underlying inventory shortage? customers reporting timeouts on model start.

maria: initial glance: many requests queued, kube-scheduler binding fails with "NoResources" for accelerator type a100. Node groups report N=0 available GPUs in the dedicated pool.

alen: adding context — we drained a decommissioned rack overnight and a few hosts didn't come back into the pool because of a firmware bug that blocks device drivers. ops ticket #3479.

maria: thanks. while ops works on firmware, we should failover traffic from dedicated-gpu-pool-3 to dedicated-gpu-pool-1 (in us-west-1 is global, but we have us-west-2->us-west-1 cross-region policy). Initiating routing change to redirect new allocation requests.

eng-runtime: note: v2 models pinned to pool-3 for performance. will fallback to compatible quantized variants if routed to pool-1. doing a compatibility check on the fly.

maria: executing routing change: 
```
redwoodctl route update --from=dedicated-gpu-pool-3 --to=dedicated-gpu-pool-1 --mode=gradual --max-pps=200
```

incident-bot: ACTION: routing rule updated, gradual switch started. Estimated time to finish: ~6m.

jessica: I've opened a customer impact note in the support dashboard for top 3 affected accounts. Customer-facing status page updated: "Degraded model start times in us-west-2. We are routing traffic to alternative capacity."

maria: autoscaler restart returned healthy, but node plugin still reports device drivers failing on 6 hosts. Ops is isolating them.

dan: monitoring shows model start latency back to baseline for new allocations, but existing warmed instances still in queue failing. We'll kick a KV-cache eviction to force restart of lingering pods in pool-3.

maria: doing eviction: `kubectl -n redwood rollout restart ds/gpu-device-plugin -l pool=dedicated-gpu-pool-3`

ops-bot: hosts in pool-3 with firmware issue: host-03, host-07, host-12. Remediation in progress (reboot+driver reflash). ETA 45m for full remediation.

sre_lead: quick ask — is cross-region burst capacity enabled for all enterprise customers? we might need to adjust routing policy for customers with strict regional binding.

jessica: noted. two enterprise customers have region lock. I've notified the AEs for those accounts and sent proposed mitigation (priority migration windows or reserved burst in us-west-1).

alen: ops update: we can bring a small batch of extra preemptible nodes in us-west-2 as short-term capacity, but that will increase latency for those instances. Recommend mixing: gradual routing + short-term preemptibles + expedited driver fix.

maria: agreed. enabling preemptible pool: `infractl scale pool dedicated-preemptible-uw2 --count +12`

incident-bot: NOTE: Preemptible pool scaled, 12 nodes requested. Estimated provisioning 3–6m.

dan: confirming customer impact windows — from 02:17 to ~02:38 some model starts failed; majority mitigated by reroute and scale at ~02:28. We should capture exact counts for postmortem.

maria: capturing timeline in incident doc: https://redwood.atlassian.com/INC-2026-1734123456 (private). adding initial notes.

sre_lead: once immediate recovery done, schedule postmortem with ops, runtime, and product next business day. I can host; propose 2026-03-16 14:00 PT.

jessica: adding postmortem invite, includes account execs for impacted customers.

maria: final status: routing complete, new allocations flowing to pool-1 and preemptible nodes in pool-2 are active. driver reflash continuing; three hosts still offline. Service impact: elevated model start latency and ~2% failed launches for 21m window.

ops-bot: host-03 returned to service at 02:54 UTC after reflash. host-07 still pending, host-12 under maintenance.

dan: follow-ups — we found autoscaler controller didn't re-evaluate pending requests after device plugin restart due to a bug in the queue drain logic. created GH issue: redwood/autoscaler#1128.

sre_lead: posting action items here. We'll track as separate tickets:
- ACTION-1: Patch autoscaler queue drain to trigger reevaluation after device plugin restarts (owner: dan, ticket: AUT-1128, due: 2026-03-20).
- ACTION-2: Add synthetic allocation surge test in us-west-2 to validate firmware/driver behavior under decomm/reboot (owner: alen, ticket: OPS-3480, due: 2026-03-24).
- ACTION-3: Increase reserved burst capacity for dedicated-gpu-pool-3 to cover 20% of baseline while firmware rollout ongoing (owner: ops team, ticket: OPS-3481, due: 2026-03-18).
- ACTION-4: Update routing playbook to include explicit steps for region-locked customers and account notification template (owner: jessica, ticket: PM-553, due: 2026-03-19).
- ACTION-5: Postmortem meeting scheduled 2026-03-16 14:00 PT (owner: sre_lead).

maria: adding minimal runbook edits now to avoid repeated manual steps. will push a follow-up PR to the runbooks repo.

eng-runtime: will prepare compatibility report for models pinned to pool-3 and list recommended fallback quantized variants so product can set expectations.

dan: quick mitigation note in GH issue: workaround is to force requeue of pending allocations:
```
# temporary mitigation
kubectl exec -n redwood statefulset/autoscaler -- /bin/sh -c "curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/reevaluate"
```

alen: ops will schedule the firmware fleet rollout and confirm when all hosts are patched. ETA fleet completion 2026-03-18.

jessica: customer comms in draft, will send update after postmortem decisions.

sre_lead: tagging owners in thread. please update your assigned ticket with notes and a plan. we'll close incident thread when postmortem is complete and actions tracked.

maria: final note for oncall handoff — @dan will take primary follow-ups for the next 12h, I'll be available for escalations. leaving oncall at 03:05 UTC.

dan: acknowledged, taking handoff. I'll consolidate logs and metrics into the postmortem doc.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: Severity downgraded to S1. Root cause: combination of firmware-induced device-driver failures + autoscaler queue drain bug. Follow-up: postmortem scheduled + action items created.

jessica: thanks team. I'll coordinate customer outbound once we have the postmortem summary. :pray:
